sections.domain: Rules of the road: first part
sections.heading: Rules of the road: first part — C
sections.markdown:
FACT_ID: sec03-F01 | anchor: A19
Posted speed limits reflect road design, expected traffic and dry, clear conditions without fog or other visibility problems. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F02 | anchor: A19
Poor weather, a bad road surface or heavy traffic can make a reasonable driving speed lower than the posted limit. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F03 | anchor: A19
Whatever the posted limit, Ohio prohibits driving faster than allows you to stop within the clear distance available ahead. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-F04 | anchor: A21
Right of way means that a pedestrian or vehicle has priority to proceed over others in a particular setting. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F05 | anchor: A21
Yield to a driver who is already at an intersection or reached it before you. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F06 | anchor: A21
When turning left, yield to drivers approaching in the opposing traffic lane. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F07 | anchor: A21
If two drivers reach a four-way intersection together, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F08 | anchor: A21
When entering a public highway from a driveway or private road, yield to traffic on the highway. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F09 | anchor: A22
A driver using an entrance or acceleration ramp must yield to vehicles already on the interstate or limited-access highway. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F10 | anchor: A22
Yield to pedestrians, bicycle riders and other drivers who remain within the intersection. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F11 | anchor: A22
Yield the right of way to public-safety vehicles such as emergency, police and fire vehicles. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F12 | anchor: A22
Yield the right of way to a funeral procession. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F13 | anchor: A22
Vertical traffic lights usually show red above yellow above green, although some signals are horizontal or show only one color. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F14 | anchor: A22
At a red light, stop before the intersection and wait behind the stop line, crosswalk or intersection boundary for green. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F15 | anchor: A22
A yellow traffic light warns that red is next; approach cautiously and prepare to stop. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F16 | anchor: A23
A green light permits cautious travel through an intersection only when the way is clear. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F17 | anchor: A23
A green arrow permits a turn in the arrow's direction without first stopping. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F18 | anchor: A23
At a flashing yellow light, reduce speed and proceed carefully, ready to stop for traffic entering the intersection. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F19 | anchor: A23
At flashing red, make a complete stop behind the stop line, crosswalk or intersection, then enter only after checking that no traffic crosses your path. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-F20 | anchor: A24
Treat a traffic light that is not operating like a stop sign, yielding and entering the intersection cautiously. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0024]

sections.domain: Rules of the road: first part
sections.heading: Rules of the road: first part — C2
sections.markdown:
FACT_ID: sec03-R01 | anchor: A24
Traffic signs communicate rules, hazards, road location, directions and nearby roadway services. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R02 | anchor: A24
A sign's shape, color, symbols and wording help identify the kind of information it conveys. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R03 | anchor: A24
Regulatory signs communicate traffic laws or regulations that govern traffic movement. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R04 | anchor: A24
Observe the posted school-zone speed restriction during the hours specified on its sign. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R05 | anchor: A25
A red circle crossed by a slash means that the action represented by the sign is forbidden. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-R06 | anchor: A25
Warning signs alert a driver to potential danger farther along the road. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-R07 | anchor: A25
Warning signs are usually diamond-shaped and yellow, with black symbols or lettering. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0025]

Confusables: green permits movement only when clear; flashing yellow requires caution, while flashing red requires a complete stop. Mnemonic: clear path before movement. Glossary: right of way means priority; regulatory signs state traffic rules; warning signs identify possible hazards. These descriptions organize the cited statements and do not replace their conditions.
